steps.content: The woman in the blue dress is sitting up straight in the interrogation room.
As usual, there's a smile on her face, just like the first time you met her.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's been a while. Sorry for causing you trouble while I was asleep.
After the Witching Hour incident was resolved, having absorbed the manic power, Enfer awakened as an S-Class Sinner. She fell into a coma and has only come back to consciousness a few days ago.
Having heard from the doctor that she's been recovering well, you decided to come and meet her.

options: Don't worry, I was just doing my job.

choices.text: Don't worry, I was just doing my job.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Your job... Haha...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That word makes our relationship sound... Quite distant.
Enfer raises her hands and gestures the distance between you and her.
Sorry. This is just a standard procedure.
I don't mean to make things difficult for you.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: No worries, me neither.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But... I don't think you came all the way here just to say hi, Chief.
Indeed, I didn't. But still, I'm glad to see that you're well.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's all thanks to you.
That's good.
I know this could seem a bit... rushed, but there are things I want to know, too, so...
If you think you can't answer these questions at this moment, we can take our time.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Go ahead. I'm not that fragile.
test
test
test
test
test
test
Here's some information about the current situation of the Belphegor Art Museum.
Although you've already absorbed the Witching Hour and I've put the shackles on you, we still haven't figured out where the Witching Hour's power came from.
Enfer stares at the documents and photos you've laid out on the desk wordlessly.
Her fingers touch the photos gently. In the photos, almost all the artwork displayed in Belphegor have been crushed into pieces.
I'm sorry. Perhaps I shouldn't have shown you these...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That's alright.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It wasn't you who broke them.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Go on.
You look at Enfer, grit your teeth, and continue.
The power of the Witching Hour was strong enough to make a regular Sinner evolve into an S-Class Sinner.
Even though I was there, I still can't figure out the origin of this power.
Its origin is unknown, the cause of evolution is unknown, and most terrifying of all... even its limit is unknown.
You must know that Eastside... has always been prejudiced against Mania. They refuse to take charge of the cleanup work in the Belphegor Art Museum.
Since we still can't fully comprehend the Witching Hour... in a sense, the fear and chaos brought by it haven't come to an end yet.
Enfer draws back her hand thumbing the photos and lifts her head to stare at you firmly.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I don't know...
But...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Before you put the shackles on me, I didn't really know what a Sinner was.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: And I have no idea why the Witching Hour's power could turn me into what you refer to as an S-Class.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But since it could cause such an outcome, perhaps it means... the Witching Hour's power is the same as a Sinner's power.
Enfer props up her face and seems to be caught up in her thoughts.
So... you mean to say that the Witching Hour's power has the same origin as a Sinner's power?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Yes... So...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Where does a Sinner's power come from?
Enfer looks at you with a faint yearning in her eyes.
You raise your hand and gesture for her to look at the blue heart-shaped accessory on her own chest.
I think Sinners' powers probably come from their own hearts.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: If you're right...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: You're the Chief, the Sinners' manager... You ought to be right.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: According to you, could it be that the Witching Hour's power came from my heart?
I think part of the Witching Hour's power came out of Parma's stones from which your sculptures were made, and part of it came from the visitors' inner fear.
As for the power to accept and absorb everything, awaken as an S-Class Sinner, and defeat the Witching Hour... That came from your heart.
Enfer gives a laugh and then falls silent again.
When Sinners... awaken, their hearts are usually filled with some kind of thought, emotion, or... desire.
Does that remind you of anything?
Enfer looks at you and laughs again.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Both you and I experienced the Witching Hour firsthand, do you still not understand?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: For me, my heart has always been yearning for fear.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That's the truth in people's hearts. That's the truth of the world.
Enfer taps on a photo on the desk. In the photo, there's a broken sculpture.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: For example, the traces of wind...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Everything in this world, even the wind, leaves its traces.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: After it spreads sickness, wails, and despair all over the world, what's left is this devilish dead branch.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: These dead branches are all around us. That's the truth told by the wind.
As Enfer pushes the photo in her hand away and is about to tell you about the truth of fear in the next photo, she halts.
The devastated sculpture in that photo is Sosia.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But Sosia... seemed to be different...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: She's indeed a piece I created. Yet, she seemed to understand me better than I do.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: She believed that I was lost and weak... She thought my fear was not pure, and that I didn't understand myself.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...She thought that I've never abandoned love, all this time.
Enfer frowns and recalls the words Sosia once shouted at her.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But... I have abandoned love such a long time ago...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I have seen how fake, how fragile, how defenseless love is...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: When the land cracks and dark clouds gather in the sky, only fear can keep us barely alive.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: How can love... still possibly exist? Or perhaps I should say... How can it possibly still exist in me?
Enfer is deep in thought again. You shake your head slightly and ask her a question.
Have you ever heard of that fable?
The North Wind and the Sun.
Enfer looks dazed for a second, then nods at you. She seems interested in your words and signals you to continue.
The North Wind and the Sun have a bet on which of them can make people take off the coat they're wearing.
No matter how hard the North Wind blows, no matter how it raises the dust and lowers the temperature, it only makes them pull the coat tighter and tighter.
Meanwhile, the sun emerges behind the clouds and shines over the land, making everyone sweat. All the passers-by wearing coats begin to take them off.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: So... you think I'm the North Wind?
I just want to tell you that, the North Wind and the wails do exist, no matter what. But they are definitely not the only things we perceive.
Even as we walk along the end... There is love, and sunshine.
Without love... how do you create these works of art that you deem as your own children?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...It's just fear.
You're lost, Enfer.
In your mind, you can feel the shackles bound on Enfer throb. Your words have made her waver.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Yes... I am indeed a little lost.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I've always thought I'm pure enough, but I can't even refute you promptly.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: What kind of thoughts and emotions was I having when I became a Sinner?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: And when I created them... Was there really... only fear?
Enfer gives a sigh, then smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: You don't know the origin of the Witching Hour, so you've come to ask the Witch.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Surprise, even the Witch doesn't know where her power comes from!
That's okay. I can look for it with you.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Huh?
You look at Enfer and give her the same smile as hers.
I've said that before. Wherever you go, I'll stay beside you.
So... If you want to find out why you're lost, where your power comes from.
I'll go with you.
Though a little surprised, Enfer accepts your kindness with a smile.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Thank you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: In that case... why don't you come with me to Belphegor?
Back to the art museum?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: If we want to find the source of the Witching Hour's power, that should be the best place to start!

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Who knows, I may be able to recall something from my past creations.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Also... Didn't you say no one dared to clean up the pieces inside?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Who else would be more suited for this job than us?
That's true.
In fact, the FAC initially wanted me and my Sinners to handle this as well.
It's just that... I must first confirm that my Sinner won't go manic under the influence of the Witching Hour again.
In other words...
You wave your hand in front of Enfer.

options: I must make sure you'll obey me.

choices.text: I must make sure you'll obey me.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Hehe...
Enfer props her chin on her palm, her eyes curving with her smile.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Am I not obedient enough, Honored Chief?
